beats.text: Two men filed for the telephone on one day.
beats.note: Alexander Graham Bell filed a patent application. Elisha Gray filed a patent caveat.

beats.name: Elisha Gray
beats.role: Filed through his lawyer, William D. Baldwin. By his account, the caveat was taken to the office hours before Bell's papers.

beats.note: Historians still disagree. Bell's fee reached the cash blotter first, but Gray's caveat may have sat unprocessed in the in-basket until the afternoon.
Bell's lawyer had his fee entered at once. Gray's went through at the usual pace, and reached the examiner the next day.
The Telephone Appeals were argued from 24 January to 8 February 1887.

beats.text: One day, two filings, and a dispute that never fully settled.

beats.line: The telephone has two birth certificates.
